userStories.title: Update migration runner to support timestamp-format filenames
userStories.description:
Modify backend/src/db/pg-index.ts to recognize both sequential (001_description.sql) and timestamp (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql) migration filename formats. The runner currently extracts the numeric prefix from filenames and uses it as the version number in schema_migrations. Since a timestamp like 20260313120000 is just a larger integer than 072, the existing ordering logic (sort by numeric prefix ascending) already handles both formats — timestamps naturally sort after sequential numbers. The key change is ensuring the regex that extracts the numeric prefix accepts both 3-digit and 14-digit prefixes, and that the migration runner does not assume any maximum prefix length. Both formats coexist indefinitely during the transition period.

## Context
- **Core change is in `backend/src/db/pg-index.ts`**: Widen the migration filename regex from fixed-width (e.g., `^(\d{3})_`) to `^(\d+)_` so both 3-digit sequential and 14-digit timestamp prefixes are extracted. Verify `parseInt()` is used — safe for 14-digit timestamps (under `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` ~9×10¹⁵).
- **Check `schema_migrations.version` column type**: If it's `INTEGER` (max ~2.1×10⁹), a 14-digit timestamp overflows. You'll need an `ALTER COLUMN version TYPE BIGINT` migration using the OLD sequential format (e.g., `073_bigint_version.sql`) **before** any timestamp-format migration can be applied. This is a blocking prerequisite.
- **Sort must be numeric, not lexicographic**: Ensure migrations sort by `parseInt(prefix)` ascending. String sort would break ordering (e.g., `"20260313"` < `"3"` lexicographically). The existing runner likely already does numeric sort — verify and preserve.
- **Known gotcha — duplicate migration numbers**: Parallel branches have collided on sequential numbers before (069 collision, 2026-03-13). Add a code comment noting that timestamp format prevents this class of collision.
- **PostgreSQL placeholder convention**: All `schema_migrations` queries must use `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders (not `?`). Preserve the existing pattern.
- **Test with Jest**: Create a test verifying both filename formats are discovered, extracted, and sorted correctly (sequential 001–072 before timestamp 20260313120000). Mock the filesystem or use a temp directory with mixed files. Reference patterns in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/`.
- **Coexistence is permanent**: Do NOT deprecate sequential format. The ~72+ existing sequential migrations will never be renamed. Both formats coexist indefinitely.
- **No operational risk**: `pg-index.ts` runs once at startup — modifying it doesn't affect active pipeline runs or require `tsx watch` restart concerns.
acceptanceCriteria: The migration runner regex in pg-index.ts accepts filenames matching both /^(\d{3})_/ (sequential) and /^(\d{14})_/ (timestamp) patterns, extracting the full numeric prefix as the version
Migrations are sorted by their numeric prefix in ascending order — timestamp-format files (e.g., 20260313120000) naturally sort after sequential files (e.g., 072)
A test file named 20260313120000_test_timestamp.sql placed in pg-migrations/ is discovered, ordered after all existing sequential migrations, and would be applied if not already in schema_migrations
The schema_migrations table stores the full numeric prefix as the version (e.g., version=20260313120000 for timestamp files, version=72 for sequential files)
Existing sequential migrations (001–072) continue to be discovered and applied without any changes to their filenames

userStories.title: Add duplicate migration prefix detection with loud failure
userStories.description:
Add a duplicate-detection check in backend/src/db/pg-index.ts that runs at startup BEFORE any migrations are applied. After scanning pg-migrations/ and extracting numeric prefixes, check for any two files sharing the same prefix. If duplicates are found, throw an error immediately with a clear message listing the conflicting filenames — do NOT silently skip one. This prevents the silent data loss that occurred with migrations 069 and 070 where parallel branches created files with the same prefix and the second was silently ignored.

## Context
- **Target file**: `backend/src/db/pg-index.ts` — insert duplicate check after the `fs.readdirSync` call that lists `pg-migrations/` files, but before the migration application loop. Do not restructure the existing runner logic.
- **Extract a testable helper**: Create `checkDuplicatePrefixes(filenames: string[]): void` as a named export from `pg-index.ts` (or a small helper module). This keeps the test (`backend/src/db/__tests__/migration-duplicates.test.ts`) filesystem-free — pass mock filename arrays directly.
- **Prefix extraction pattern**: Files follow `NNN_description.sql`. Use regex `/^(\d+)_/` to extract the numeric prefix. Parse to integer for grouping (`Map<number, string[]>`). Zero-padded prefixes like `001` and `1` should collide (same integer), though in practice all files use 3-digit zero-padded prefixes.
- **Error convention**: Use `throw new Error(...)` — NOT `console.error` + `process.exit(1)`. The migration runner runs during backend startup; an uncaught throw halts the process and surfaces in logs. Error message must contain the word "duplicate" (case-insensitive) and list all conflicting filenames with their prefix number.
- **Known incident context**: Duplicate migration 069 collision (2026-03-13) — two parallel dev branches both created `069_*.sql`, runner silently skipped the second, causing missing schema. This is the direct fix. See MEMORY.md "No migration number enforcement" process gap.
- **Happy path = zero overhead**: Single `readdirSync` (already happens) + one pass grouping. No additional logging or delay when no duplicates exist. Currently 72+ migration files (001–074).
- **Test file**: `backend/src/db/__tests__/migration-duplicates.test.ts` using Jest. Test cases: (1) throws on duplicate prefixes with message containing both filenames, (2) succeeds silently on unique prefixes, (3) handles edge case of 3+ files sharing one prefix.
- **PostgreSQL gotcha**: DB uses `$1, $2` numbered placeholders — not relevant here since this is filesystem-only, but keep in mind if touching any SQL in the same file.
acceptanceCriteria: When two migration files share the same numeric prefix (e.g., 069_foo.sql and 069_bar.sql), the migration runner throws an Error at startup with a message containing both filenames and the conflicting prefix number
The duplicate check runs BEFORE any pending migrations are applied — no migrations execute if duplicates are detected
The error message format includes the word 'DUPLICATE' or 'duplicate' and lists all conflicting filenames so developers can immediately identify which files to rename
When no duplicates exist, the migration runner proceeds normally with no additional logging or delay
A backend Jest test in a new file backend/src/db/__tests__/migration-duplicates.test.ts verifies that the runner throws on duplicate prefixes and succeeds when prefixes are unique

userStories.title: Create automated rename script for existing sequential migrations
userStories.description:
Create backend/scripts/rename-migrations.ts — a standalone TypeScript script (runnable via npx tsx backend/scripts/rename-migrations.ts) that renames all existing sequential migration files (001–072) in backend/src/db/pg-migrations/ to timestamp format. The timestamp for each file is estimated based on git blame (first commit date of the file) or falls back to a monotonically increasing timestamp starting from 20260101000000 if git blame is unavailable. The script must be idempotent — running it twice produces no changes on the second run. It outputs a mapping of old filename → new filename for verification before committing.

## Context
- **Read `pg-index.ts` sort behavior first**: The migration runner in `backend/src/db/pg-index.ts` sorts filenames lexicographically — confirm it doesn't `parseInt()` the prefix, which would collapse leading zeros on 14-digit timestamps. This is a blocking prerequisite before any rename logic.
- **`schema_migrations` table gap is critical**: The `schema_migrations` table stores the migration filename as its tracking key. Renaming files on disk without updating those rows will cause the runner to re-execute all migrations on next startup (destructive). The script must output a companion SQL `UPDATE` statement mapping old → new filenames, or document this clearly in stdout. Do NOT silently rename without addressing this.
- **Handle non-contiguous numbering**: Memory confirms duplicate `069` collision (parallel branches, renamed to `071`). The actual sequence may be `001–068, 070, 071, 072` — sort by numeric prefix extraction (`parseInt(filename.match(/^(\d{3})_/)[1])`), never assume sequential continuity.
- **Git blame with `--follow` and `--diff-filter=A`**: Use `git log --follow --format=%at --diff-filter=A -- <filepath>` taking the last line (earliest add commit). Some files moved from SQLite-era directories. For untracked files visible in `git status` (e.g., `072_`, `073_`, `074_`), use monotonic fallback timestamps strictly greater than all git-derived ones.
- **Deduplicate same-commit timestamps**: Multiple migrations committed in one commit share the same unix timestamp. Add 1-second increments per file within the same timestamp, ordered by numeric prefix, to guarantee strict monotonicity. Never let a higher-numbered migration receive an earlier timestamp.
- **Test strategy**: Place tests at `backend/scripts/__tests__/rename-migrations.test.ts`. Use `fs.mkdtempSync` for temp directory with mock files. Mock `child_process.execSync` for git blame. Assert: sequential files renamed, already-converted files untouched, second run is no-op, `--dry-run` prints but doesn't rename. Backend uses Jest (not Vitest).
- **No external dependencies**: Use only `fs`, `path`, `child_process`. Parse `--dry-run` via `process.argv.includes('--dry-run')` — no CLI parser libraries.
acceptanceCriteria: Running npx tsx backend/scripts/rename-migrations.ts renames all files matching /^\d{3}_/ in backend/src/db/pg-migrations/ to /^\d{14}_/ format, preserving the description suffix (e.g., 001_initial_schema.sql → 20260101000001_initial_schema.sql)
Timestamps are monotonically increasing — migration 002 always gets a timestamp greater than 001, preserving execution order
The script prints a table of old filename → new filename mappings to stdout before performing renames, and accepts a --dry-run flag that prints the mapping without renaming
Running the script a second time (when files are already in timestamp format) produces no renames and exits cleanly with a message like 'No sequential migrations found to rename'
Files already in timestamp format (14-digit prefix) are left untouched by the script

userStories.title: Update schema_migrations table entries after rename
userStories.description:
After US-003 renames the migration files, the schema_migrations table still has rows referencing the old filenames (if a filename column exists) or old version numbers. This story ensures the schema_migrations table is consistent with the new filenames. If schema_migrations only stores the numeric version (e.g., 1, 2, ... 72), update each row's version to the corresponding timestamp number (e.g., 1 → 20260101000001, 72 → the timestamp assigned to migration 072). The rename script from US-003 should output the version mapping, and this story adds a SQL migration or script step that applies that mapping to schema_migrations. This must be done in a transaction so that a partial failure doesn't leave schema_migrations in an inconsistent state.

## Context
- **Read `backend/src/db/pg-index.ts` first** — this is the migration runner and the sole authority on how `schema_migrations` tracks applied migrations. Determine the exact column name (`version`, `name`, `filename`), data type (`TEXT` vs `INTEGER`), and how the runner sorts/compares entries (lexicographic on filename vs numeric on prefix). Timestamp prefixes (14 digits) sort correctly lexicographically but may overflow if the column is `INTEGER` — confirm it's `TEXT` or `BIGINT`.

- **Use a dedicated pg client for transactional updates** — `const client = await pool.connect()` with `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` in try/catch/finally. Never use `pool.query()` for multi-statement transactions (each call may use a different connection). Use `$1, $2` numbered placeholders, not `?`.

- **Consume the version mapping from US-003's rename script output** — expect a JSON file (e.g., `backend/scripts/migration-version-map.json`) with `{"old_prefix": "new_timestamp_prefix", ...}`. Do not hardcode mappings. Account for the known 069→071 collision: parallel dev branches both used 069, one was manually renamed to 071, so the mapping must reflect actual before/after values on disk.

- **Idempotency is critical** — before updating, check if values are already in timestamp format (e.g., values > 20000000000000 or filenames matching `/^\d{14}/`). Exit cleanly with a log message if already migrated. This prevents errors on re-runs and is an explicit AC.

- **Post-update verification step before COMMIT** — run `SELECT version FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version ASC` within the same transaction and compare against `ls backend/src/db/pg-migrations/ | sort` to confirm 1:1 order match. Log mismatches as errors and ROLLBACK if any discrepancy is found.

- **Jest tests required** (`test: true` in engineering standards) — create a test file that: (1) mocks `schema_migrations` with old sequential versions, runs the update, asserts timestamp versions; (2) tests the idempotent no-op path; (3) simulates a failure mid-update and verifies full rollback. Use `jest.mock` for the DB client or wrap in a test transaction that rolls back.

- **Known codebase pattern** — migrations are SQL files in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` (currently 001–074 based on git status showing up to 074). The runner in `pg-index.ts` tracks them in `schema_migrations`. New migration files use sequential numbering — this story converts that to timestamp numbering, so confirm no other code depends on sequential integer ordering.
acceptanceCriteria: After running the update, every row in schema_migrations has a version value matching the new timestamp-format numeric prefix of its corresponding migration file
The update is performed inside a single database transaction — if any row update fails, all changes are rolled back
A verification query (SELECT version FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version ASC) shows versions in the same order as the renamed migration files sorted alphabetically
The update script or migration handles the case where schema_migrations is already up-to-date (idempotent — no error if versions already match timestamp format)

The rename script from US-003 is extended to also run this schema_migrations update step, or a companion script backend/scripts/update-schema-versions.ts is created that reads the mapping and applies it

userStories.title: Update CLAUDE.md with timestamp migration format documentation
userStories.description:
Update the CLAUDE.md file at the repository root to document the new timestamp-based migration filename format. Replace any references to sequential numbering (001, 002, etc.) with the new YYYYMMDDHHMMSS format. Explain WHY the format changed (collision prevention on parallel branches — reference the 069/070 incidents). Include the exact command to generate a new migration filename: date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S. Update the 'PostgreSQL Migration Pattern' section in CLAUDE.md and any other sections that reference migration file naming conventions.

## Context
- **Scope is documentation-only**: Edit `CLAUDE.md` (repo root) and `AGENTS.md` (repo root) only. Do NOT touch any `.sql` migration files, `pg-index.ts`, or other source code.
- **CLAUDE.md has multiple stale migration references**: The "PostgreSQL Migration Pattern" section says "49 files, 001–049" and the "Database Tables" header says "62 migrations (001–062)". Search globally for patterns like `001–0`, `NNN_`, `numeric order`, `pg-migrations/` count references, and `New migrations: create` to catch all instances. There are at least 3 distinct locations that need updating.
- **Transition boundary**: Existing migrations `001_` through `074_` keep their sequential `NNN_` prefix — only NEW migrations use `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`. Make this explicit to prevent confusion (nobody should rename existing files).

- **Lexicographic sort safety**: `pg-index.ts` sorts filenames lexicographically. 14-digit `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` timestamps sort AFTER all `0XX_` prefixed files (digit `2` > digit `0`), so no ordering conflict. Mention this so readers understand why the mixed format works.

Also confirm no migration files were accidentally modified with `git diff --name-only`.

userStories.title: Update L3 direction stack with current migration timestamp context
userStories.description:
Update the L3 direction stack for the rorca workspace (via the direction_layers table or rorca_update_direction API) to inject the current migration timestamp as context. This ensures that when agents generate new migrations during spec execution, they use the correct timestamp format and never collide with existing migrations. The L3 content should include a section like: 'New migrations MUST use timestamp prefix format: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql. Generate the prefix with: date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S. The highest existing migration timestamp as of this writing is XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX — always use a timestamp greater than this.' The highest timestamp value must be dynamically determined from the current migration files at the time of the direction stack update.

## Context
- **Preserve existing L3 content**: Read current L3 via `rorca_get_direction` or `GET /api/direction?workspaceId=rorca&layer=3` before updating. The L3 layer contains stack, architecture, and constraints YAML — merging a new `migrations:` section into existing content is required. Overwriting will destroy project context.
- **Migration file discovery**: Glob `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/*.sql` to find all files. Current files use mixed formats: old sequential (`001_` through `074_`) and potentially timestamp-prefixed. Extract all numeric prefixes, sort numerically, and report the highest. As of git status, `074_add_memories_embedding_column.sql` appears to be the highest — but scan at runtime, never hardcode.
- **Deprecation language must be explicit**: The L3 section must state that `NNN_description.sql` sequential numbering is permanently deprecated. Reference the known duplicate migration `069` collision bug as justification. Only `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql` is valid for new migrations.
- **Include shell command**: Add `date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S` as the canonical way to generate timestamp prefixes. This removes ambiguity for implementing agents about timezone or format.
- **Synthesis verification**: After updating L3, call `rorca_synthesize_direction` (or `GET /api/direction/synthesize`) and assert the migration guidance appears in the merged output. L3 is project-scoped and should not be overridden by L1/L2 global layers — but verify this explicitly.
- **Use `rorca_update_direction` with `contentYaml` param**: The update tool expects valid YAML as `contentYaml`. Ensure the migration section is properly formatted YAML (not raw markdown) so it parses correctly in the direction stack. Test that the YAML round-trips through `synthesize()` without corruption.
- **Jest test**: Write a test in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/direction.test.ts` (or a new file) that queries `direction_layers` for the rorca workspace L3 layer and asserts the migration timestamp section exists. Use `$1, $2` pg placeholders, `await` all DB calls. The test should verify both the format guidance string and the presence of a numeric "highest migration" value.
- **DB column gotcha**: `direction_layers` table uses standard column names (`content`, `layer`, `workspace_id`, `domain`). No `ts`/`created_at` confusion here — that's only `wal_events`. But if writing WAL-based assertions in tests, use `ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: The L3 direction layer for the rorca workspace contains a migration naming section that specifies the YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql format
The L3 content includes the highest existing migration timestamp number so agents know the minimum value for new migrations
The direction stack update is applied via the rorca_update_direction MCP tool or direct API call to PUT /api/direction
After the update, calling rorca_synthesize_direction for the rorca workspace includes the migration timestamp guidance in the synthesized output
The L3 migration section explicitly states that sequential numbering (001, 002, etc.) is deprecated and must not be used for new migrations

userStories.title: Add Jest integration tests for migration timestamp system
userStories.description:
Create a comprehensive Jest integration test suite at backend/src/db/__tests__/migration-system.test.ts that validates the complete migration timestamp system end-to-end using mock file systems and mock DB connections (safe for CI). Tests must cover: (1) migration runner sorting — both 3-digit (001) and 14-digit (20260313120000) prefixes are accepted and sorted correctly (timestamps always after sequentials when both exist); (2) duplicate prefix detection — duplicate 3-digit or 14-digit prefixes throw an Error with a message containing the duplicate prefix and the conflicting filenames; (3) rename script dry-run mode — output mapping matches expected old→new filename pairs without writing any files; (4) schema_migrations UPDATE — idempotent on re-run (second apply produces no rows changed) and wrapped in a transaction (rolled back on error); (5) direction stack L3 synthesis — synthesize() output includes the string 'timestamp' and migration format guidance when L3 content references migration conventions. Use jest.mock for fs/promises and pg Pool. No real files or DB connections.

## Context
- **Test file location**: `backend/src/db/__tests__/migration-system.test.ts` — new file. Backend tests use Jest (not Vitest). Run with `npx jest --testPathPattern=migration-system`.
- **Migration runner lives at `backend/src/db/pg-index.ts`**: This is the migration runner that reads `pg-migrations/`, sorts files, tracks applied migrations in `schema_migrations` table, and runs each inside a transaction. Mock its `fs.readdirSync`/`fs.readFileSync` and `pg` Pool calls.
- **PostgreSQL conventions**: All DB calls use `pg` Pool with `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders (not `?`). `await query<T>(sql, params)` returns `T[]`, `await execute(sql, params)` returns `{ rowCount }`. Mock the Pool/Client interface accordingly.
- **Duplicate migration collision is a real bug**: Migration 069 collision happened on 2026-03-13 (parallel dev branches). The duplicate detection test validates the fix. Ensure the error message includes both filenames so developers can identify which branches conflicted.
- **Direction stack synthesis**: `synthesize()` in `backend/src/lib/direction-stack.ts` merges L1→L5 into a single context string. For the L3 test, mock `direction_layers` DB query to return L3 content containing migration format text, then assert the synthesized output includes `'timestamp'`.
- **No real DB or filesystem**: All tests must use `jest.mock('fs/promises')` and mock `pg` Pool/Client. The test suite must be CI-safe — no Docker, no Postgres connection, no temp files on disk.
- **Existing test patterns**: Check `backend/src/routes/__tests__/*.test.ts` for the project's Jest mock patterns — they mock `db/index.ts` query helpers extensively. Follow the same `jest.mock('../../db')` pattern for consistency.
- **Rename script**: The migration rename script (sequential→timestamp) may live in `backend/src/db/` or as a standalone script. Search with `Grep` for `rename` + `migration` to locate it before writing the dry-run test. If it doesn't exist yet (planned by the spec), write the test against the expected interface described in the AC.

When two feature branches independently create migrations, they silently collide on the same number — the migration runner (pg-index.ts) applies the first and silently skips the second, permanently losing schema changes with no error. This happened twice in production: 069 and 070 both had two competing migrations from parallel branches. The fix is timestamp-based migration filenames using the format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql (e.g., 20260313120000_add_source_to_memories.sql). This spec: (1) Updates the migration runner (backend/src/db/pg-index.ts) to support timestamp-format filenames alongside the existing sequential format, ordering all migrations by their numeric prefix (timestamp is just a larger number) — both formats coexist during transition; (2) Adds a duplicate-detection check in pg-index.ts that FAILS LOUDLY at startup if two migration files share the same numeric prefix, throwing an error with the conflicting filenames rather than silently skipping; (3) Renames all existing sequential migration files (001–072) to timestamp format based on a best-estimate timestamp, via an automated rename script at backend/scripts/rename-migrations.ts; (4) Updates the schema_migrations table entries to match the new filenames after rename (the version column stays as the number, only filename column changes); (5) Updates CLAUDE.md to document the new timestamp migration format and explains why (collision prevention on parallel branches); (6) Updates the L3 direction stack for the rorca workspace to inject the current migration timestamp as context so that agents always generate unique migration names.
